concept: The Woven Specimen: a tactile, engraved study of a proof-bearing Web. Fine crossings and material detail carry its identity, without a character, machine, or glowing network.
composition: Use a square master with the full central weave inside a generous crop-safe area; portrait crops should trim only outer filaments. Place visual weight slightly right to echo the existing portrait panel, with charcoal margins. Keep the key crossings clear at thumbnail size so mobile square crops remain legible without text or edge detail.
strands: Give each continuous path a readable route: warm-ivory fibers and muted brass filaments pass over and under at measured crossings, looping and continuing with varied curvature. Selective engraved collars mark a few joins without creating bead-like nodes or a single hub. The weave feels coherent while each Strand remains traceable as evidence for a claim; no path implies an execution order.
brandConnection: Use charcoal #14130f, warm ivory #f0ede4, and restrained antique gold. Matte blackened metal, abraded gilt, and fine paper grain suggest Victorian mathematical craft. A faint etched crescent-star can sit behind the weave.
avoid: No people, words, pseudoletters, neon, flare, city, spider, circuits, node bubbles, arrows, fixed Strand count, three-proof grouping, seven-step sequence, checklist, or automatic-execution imagery.
imagePrompt: Square editorial artwork for Moriarty Webs and Strands: an individually traceable, coherent proof-bearing weave as a refined Victorian specimen engraving. Warm-ivory fibers and muted antique-brass filaments cross over and under in varied loops and natural tension; a few tiny engraved collars mark joins. Matte charcoal #14130f, ivory #f0ede4, restrained aged gold, subtle paper grain, blackened metal, controlled warm side light, crisp lines, quiet margins. Keep the central weave within the middle 70 percent for portrait and square crops; legible as a small website image. Optional faint crescent-star engraving. No text, people, glow, neon, spider, circuitry, node bubbles, arrows, fixed count, or sequential flow.
